# `fingerprint`

the identification of individuals across a cohort from two stored measurements each (brain fingerprinting), with the correlation, accuracy, self-identifiability, edgewise reliability and the PCA reconstruction curve.

Version 1, scope `group`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run fingerprint --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run fingerprint --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run fingerprint --dataset <folder> --subjects S01,S02,S03 --target fp_B --database fp_A
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `target` | statistic any, per_subject true, where {"name": "$target"} (each member's target (validation) feature, found by name) | yes |
| `database` | statistic any, per_subject true, where {"name": "$database"} (each member's database (training) feature, found by name) | yes |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `subjects` | `--subjects` | none | - |  | the cohort's members, by name, in order (A,B,C); no default: a group run without them is refused |
| `target` | `--target` | `required` | - |  | the stored feature identified (the release's validation half): its name in every member |
| `database` | `--database` | `required` | - |  | the stored feature it is identified against (the release's training half): its name in every member |
| `vector` | `--vector` | `flatten` | - | flatten, upper-triangle | flatten = the stored values as they are, row-major (a region x bin spectrum) \| upper-triangle = per trailing slice (band) the upper triangle WITH the diagonal of the leading square (a connectome), slices concatenated |
| `self_identifiability` | `--self-identifiability` | `all` | - | all, others | D_self: all = each correlation row z-scored over all its entries, the member included (the release's notebooks; the published numbers) \| others = the paper's formula, over the other members |
| `steps` | `--steps` | `notebook` | components |  | the numbers of components of the PCA reconstruction: notebook = 2, 5, then 10, 20, ... below 2n (the release's) \| a list of integers |
| `name` | `--name` | `fingerprint` | - |  | the stem of the stored statistics |

## The chain of nodes

| phase | node | in | with | out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | [`stats.featureTable`](../nodes.md) | target=target, database=database | vector=$vector | table |
| before | [`stats.identification`](../nodes.md) | table=table | self_identifiability=$self_identifiability | correlation, self, accuracy, edgewise |
| before | [`stats.pca`](../nodes.md) | x=table | members=measurement, scale=none | components, scores, variance, centring |
| before | [`stats.identificationCurve`](../nodes.md) | components=components, scores=scores, centring=centring | steps=$steps, self_identifiability=$self_identifiability | curve, reconstructed_self, reconstructed_edgewise |

`before` steps run once, `chunks` steps run on every chunk of the recording, `after` steps run once on what the chunks accumulated.

## Outputs

| output | stored as |
|---|---|
| `correlation` | kind statistic, name $name_correlation, of target, axes [{"name": "target_member"}, {"name": "database_member"}] |
| `self` | kind statistic, name $name_self, of target, axes [{"name": "member"}, {"name": "quantity"}] |
| `accuracy` | kind statistic, name $name_accuracy, of target, axes [{"name": "quantity"}] |
| `edgewise` | kind statistic, name $name_edgewise, of target, axes [{"name": "feature"}, {"name": "quantity"}] |
| `curve` | kind statistic, name $name_curve, of target, axes [{"name": "step"}, {"name": "quantity"}] |
| `reconstructed_self` | kind statistic, name $name_reconstructed_self, of target, axes [{"name": "member"}, {"name": "quantity"}] |
| `reconstructed_edgewise` | kind statistic, name $name_reconstructed_edgewise, of target, axes [{"name": "feature"}, {"name": "quantity"}] |
| `components` | kind statistic, name $name_pca, of target, axes [{"name": "component"}, {"name": "feature"}] |
| `scores` | kind statistic, name $name_pca_scores, of target, axes [{"name": "member"}, {"name": "component"}] |
| `variance` | kind statistic, name $name_pca_variance, of target, axes [{"name": "component"}, {"name": "quantity"}] |
| `centring` | kind statistic, name $name_pca_centring, of target, axes [{"name": "quantity"}, {"name": "feature"}] |

## Notes from the definition

```text
MEG BRAIN FINGERPRINTING, THE COHORT STATISTICS (spec docs/specs/2026-11-16-meg-fingerprinting.md, section 11.4, steps 20-25, and its amendment of 2026-11-19: the published method is the default).
The method: da Silva Castanheira J, Orozco Perez HD, Misic B, Baillet S (2021) Brief segments of neurophysiological activity enable individual differentiation. Nat Commun 12:5713,
doi:10.1038/s41467-021-25895-8; its authors' release megFingerprinting v1.0.0 (06fdba8), the notebooks 4_PSD_fingerprinting_* and 4_AEC_fingerprinting_*; the identification statistics after
Finn ES et al. (2015) Nat Neurosci 18:1664 and Amico E, Goni J (2018) Sci Rep 8:8254. Every stored result carries this citation (producer_json.references).

GROUP scope: each member's two stored features, the TARGET (the release's validation half) and the DATABASE (its training half), are found by name in every member (`--target`, `--database`:
the names the caller gave the per-subject runs, the same in every member; a member missing either is refused by name; every member's feature has one shape and the same axes, else refused).
The runner reads them into a members x features table (preparation, never a node). The graph:
  stats.featureTable          the feature vectors: flatten (a region x bin spectrum, row-major, raw values) or upper-triangle (a connectome: per band the upper triangle WITH its diagonal,
                              bands concatenated); [target; database] stacked, 2n x p
  stats.identification        each vector z-scored across its features (ddof 0); the target x database Pearson matrix; the accuracy both ways (argmax per row, per column); D_self per member
                              (`all`: the notebook's, over all n entries; `others`: the paper's formula); the edgewise ICC(1,1), Finn's differential power and the group consistency
  stats.pca                   the across-member PCA of the stacked table: an EXACT thin SVD of the centred table (the release's scikit-learn PCA(k) is randomised and unseeded at this size,
                              so its numbers are matched only to that solver's tolerance)
  stats.identificationCurve   reconstruction at each k with the mean, accuracy both ways and the mean D_self; the best k (largest mean D_self); the edgewise statistics and D_self at it
Stored in the dataset's template (format 56: the template holds the cohort), each a statistic of method `fingerprint` (the PCA's of method `pca`), OF the first member's target
(the members and each one's inputs are in the provenance), names `<name>_correlation`, `_self`, `_accuracy`, `_edgewise`, `_curve`, `_reconstructed_self`, `_reconstructed_edgewise`, `_pca*`.
It cannot show: why the two measurements of a person are alike (anatomy, head position, the kernel, recurring artefacts and the day's noise are individual too); accuracy falls as the cohort
grows and depends on its make-up, so it is not comparable between cohorts; the curve and its best k are fitted on the data they score (optimistic); the edgewise statistics are on features
z-scored within each vector (a feature's place in a person's profile, not its absolute value); neighbouring regions share signal through the kernel, so the features are far fewer
independent measurements than their number.

  nxr-neuro run fingerprint --dataset <folder> --subjects S01,S02,S03 --target fp_B --database fp_A
```
